artworks.title: Statue of Podalirius
artworks.description: A standing statue identified as Podalirius — the Asclepiad physician of the Trojan War, brother of Machaon. Reception sculpture keeps the healer-prince visible where vase-painters rarely named him alone.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Homer's Catalogue and battle books name Podalirius with Machaon as the two sons of Asclepius who heal the Achaeans — the physician-princes of the Trojan War.

popCulture.title: Podalirius
popCulture.description: Son of Asclepius who cured Philoctetes' wound in later epic — the healer whose name still marks medicine beside his father's staff.

popCulture.title: Asclepius
popCulture.description: Podalirius belongs to the Asclepiad line — brother of Machaon, heir to the healing art that Homer places in the Greek camp at Troy.

popCulture.title: Iphiclides podalirius
popCulture.description: The scarce swallowtail butterfly still carries Podalirius' name — a Linnaean afterlife for the Trojan healer.
